queries_run: Texas Instruments analog chip market share gaining OR losing 2026
Texas Instruments China analog competitor market share 2026
Texas Instruments price cuts Chinese analog vendors 2026 impact

findings.claim: TI held an estimated 17.8%-19% share of the global analog semiconductor market in 2025, the industry-leading position ahead of ADI and Infineon.

TI began production at the first module of its Sherman, TX 300mm fab in December 2025 (65nm/130nm analog nodes for smartphone power-management ICs) and announced in February 2026 a second cleanroom module adding 20,000 wafer starts/month by 2028, expanding low-cost in-house capacity ahead of the industry.
findings.source: BingX/TI newsroom coverage of Sherman fab expansion

findings.claim: Over the past five years, Chinese domestic analog vendors (e.g., SG Micro, 3Peak) have gradually eroded overseas incumbents' (including TI's) share in telecom and consumer-electronics segments, driven by geopolitical friction and China's domestic-substitution push, though their overlap is concentrated in TI's mid-to-low-end part numbers rather than the full portfolio.
findings.source: Chinese analog chip vendors brace for impact as Texas Instruments slashes prices (jw.ijiwei.com); Citrini Research "Semis Memo: Supply Chain Inheritance"

findings.claim: TI, NXP and Infineon raised analog IC prices effective April 2026 (TI hikes up to 85% on select parts), and TI announced a third sweeping price increase in May 2026 effective July 1, 2026. Analysts flagged that end customers seeking to avoid TI's price hikes may accelerate adoption of Chinese domestic alternatives, especially in long-cycle industrial and automotive sectors.
findings.source: BigGo Finance: "Texas Instruments' Third Price Hike in Six Months Ignites New Analog Chip Cycle, Opening Triple-Bonanza Window for China's Domestic Substitution"

findings.claim: Hudson Labs' 2026 TXN peer comparison notes TI has recently gained share in China (roughly 22% of TI's total revenue) even as local Chinese competition becomes faster and more capable, describing the China dynamic as a net share gain for TI so far.

note: Mixed picture: TI holds/extends #1 global analog share and is gaining in China near-term, but Chinese domestic vendors (SG Micro, 3Peak) are structurally eroding share in overlapping mid/low-end telecom & consumer segments, and TI's 2026 price hikes create an opening analysts flag as accelerating customer migration to local alternatives in industrial/auto.
